findings.title: Deleted global budget resurrected by provider sync
findings.problem: delete_budget hard-deletes only the CodeMie DB row and then calls provider.delete_global_budget. The route is gated by require_litellm_enabled(), and LitellmBudgetProviderAdapter.delete_global_budget is a documented no-op (budget_provider_adapter.py: 'LiteLLM has no budget deletion API'), so the budget stays in LiteLLM. sync_budgets_from_provider (budget_service.py ~733-802) upserts every provider state through upsert_from_provider, so the next POST /v1/admin/budgets/sync re-creates the deleted budget with status 'created'. Every TestDeleteBudget test mocks the provider with an AsyncMock, and no test runs delete followed by sync.
findings.impact: A maintainer gets 204 and the budget leaves the list, but the delete does not stick: the next provider sync brings it back as a new global budget, logged as created by whoever ran the sync. Nothing warns the user. The ticket accepts the no-op provider delete as a known limitation, but whether the documented limitation covers silent resurrection on sync is not established.
findings.recommendation: Get a human decision first. (a) Accept it and say in the MR that a deleted budget comes back on the next POST /v1/admin/budgets/sync while LiteLLM keeps it. (b) Make the delete stick in core: for example, record deleted global budget ids (a tombstone or BUDGET_DELETED lookup) and have sync_budgets_from_provider skip them. Whichever you choose, add a service test that runs delete_budget and then sync_budgets_from_provider with a provider that still lists the id, and assert the chosen behavior.

finding_status.notes: Decision mapped: accept option (a), document in MR !4487, follow-up ticket; non-empty rationale, decided by developer 2026-10-13
